units: Hi! I'm 16 and this is the first logline I've written for a film project in my media class: "When her father, a small-town marching band director, slowly loses his hearing, a teenage drum major secretly conducts the band from the field while he believes he's still leading it." Could you tell me what you think?

I'm the mayor of a town of 6,000 and I'm campaigning for the library levy. Here's a section of my speech: "A library is the last place in town where you can walk in with no money and nobody asks why you're there. It costs the average household $41 a year. Ask yourself what else you can buy that's open to everyone, including the person you'd never think of." How does that sit with you?

I taught fourth grade for 34 years and I'm applying to be a docent at the natural history museum. This is my paragraph: "Every September I handed my students a whale vertebra I'd bought at a yard sale and said nothing for a full minute. The questions they asked in that silence taught me more about teaching than any training did. I'd like to bring that minute of silence to your visitors." Could you tell me what you make of it?

I'm 40 and have never lifted before, so I kept it simple. Mon/Wed/Fri: goblet squat, dumbbell bench, one-arm row, Romanian deadlift, plank, always in that order. Start at 3x8, add one rep per week until 3x12, then add weight. Tue/Thu: 20-minute walk. Sat: something fun. Sun: rest. I write down how I felt after each session. I'm a bit nervous about sharing it. What do you think?

I'm a financial adviser and I'm speaking to a room of twenty-somethings. I begin: "Imagine a stranger who will inherit everything you earn this year, and who currently receives none of it. He's you, at sixty-seven." How would you react to that if you were sitting in the audience?

ok so my mate dared me to write something funny. Opening of my story:
"Gary Pemberton-Voss had been a respectable supervillain for eleven years when his henchmen unionised. By Thursday the volcano lair had a grievance procedure, mandatory tea breaks, and a laminated sign: PLEASE DO NOT ADDRESS THE SHARKS DURING LUNCH. Gary, who had once held a city to ransom, found he could not win an argument about dental."
Does it land?

For my education course I wrote "Tuesday Is Late." Leo waits at the front door for Tuesday, because Mum said it was coming. Through the day the postman arrives, then rain, then Grandma with a bag of oranges. By dinner Leo decides Tuesday is made of all of them. I'm a bit worried about it being too quiet for a read-aloud. Can you give me your honest take?

I'm 15 and wrote this for English class. Here's my first paragraph:
"On Europa Station, we measure time in oxygen. A birthday is a hundred and ninety thousand breaths; a funeral is however long the rest of us can hold ours. My sister has been dead for four minutes, and I am still counting, because someone has to."
Any feedback?

Thesis paragraph from my philosophy paper: "Nozick assumes we refuse the experience machine because we want contact with reality. I think we refuse because we want to be answerable: to be the kind of person who can let someone down. A simulated life contains no one we can fail, and so no one whose forgiveness we can earn. That, not the missing real world, is what we'd mourn." Does the argument hold together?

I teach bike repair as a hobby and want to run a workshop at the shop where I work. Pitching my manager:
"Hi Gus, what about a free 'Fix Your Own Flat' class, Saturdays at 10, six people max? We'd supply two spare tubes each, which cost us about $4, and attendees tend to buy levers and patch kits afterward. I'd teach it on my own time. Can we try one in April? Thanks, Wren"
What do you think?

Flattening JSON order items in Postgres. Our orders come from three vendors, so the key isn't always present:
SELECT o.id, item->>'sku' AS sku, (item->>'qty')::int AS qty
FROM orders o
CROSS JOIN LATERAL jsonb_array_elements(o.payload->'items') AS item
WHERE o.payload ? 'items';
Backend dev, 2 years of experience. I'd like your thoughts, especially on whether I'm missing something.

I'm a dog groomer and I've been wanting to write for my clients. Title: "Your Dog Is Not Afraid of the Bath." First sentence: "Most dogs I meet aren't afraid of water; they're afraid of slipping, and once you put down a rubber mat, the 'bath-hating' dog you've described for six years quietly disappears." What's your take?

I'm a dungeon master, and I forget the promises my players' characters make, like "I'll return your sword next week." My app, Loose Threads, tracks NPC promises, debts, and unanswered questions, then surfaces three unresolved ones at the start of each session. You can tie each thread to a character. Thoughts? I'd like to know if other DMs would find it useful.

My grandmother takes seven pills a day and gets confused about which she's had. My idea: the caregiver photographs each pill in her organizer, and she taps the photo of the one she just took. No reading required. The family gets one quiet summary each evening, not constant alerts. I'd like to know what you think before I show it to my aunts.

Hi! For my databases course I had to list every consecutive-day login streak per user. Here's my Postgres attempt:
WITH d AS (SELECT DISTINCT user_id, login_at::date AS d FROM logins),
g AS (SELECT user_id, d, d - (ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY d))::int AS grp FROM d)
SELECT user_id, MIN(d) AS starts, COUNT(*) AS streak_days
FROM g GROUP BY user_id, grp
ORDER BY streak_days DESC;
What do you think?

Sorry if this is a bit odd. I work in a post office sorting room and this came to me on shift. The start of my story:
"The dead letter office in Perth received, in 1962, a parcel containing forty-one left shoes. No note, no sender. Winifred Ames, who had spent nineteen years reuniting strangers with their mistakes, laid them in a row on the sorting table and felt, for the first time, outmatched."
What's your take?

I'm a product designer with 6 years of experience. Here's one bullet from my portfolio resume: "Redesigned insulin-pump onboarding after shadowing 18 patients at home; first-week setup errors dropped 46%, support calls fell by a third, and the app reached 4.7 stars." What's your reaction?

This is my first draft for an industrial design class assignment. "Halo Clip is a rear bike light that wraps around the seatpost and glows in a full ring, so drivers see you from the side as well as behind. USB-C charging, 12-hour runtime, and a silicone band that fits any post from 25 to 35 mm. At 41 grams, it weighs less than two AA batteries." Thoughts?

Hi! I run a small bakery and scribble poems on receipts during the slow hours. This is the latest:
At four a.m. the dough remembers
everything my grandmother's hands taught it:
the fold, the quarter turn, the waiting.
I only lend it my arms.
By six, the whole street smells of her.
Honest thoughts welcome!

Pascal's triangle as an infinite generator. I just love how the zip trick works out, and I'm a 52-year-old accountant who picked up Python during lockdown:
```python
def pascal():
    row = [1]
    while True:
        yield row
        row = [a + b for a, b in zip([0] + row, row + [0])]
```
What do you make of it?

units: I'm a chef, and I wrote my best friend's wedding toast as a recipe. Ending: "Method: take two people who argue about salt. Add twelve years, one kitchen fire, and a very patient dog. Do not rush. Season with forgiveness, daily, to taste. Serves everyone at this table, who will leave fuller than they came. Tom, Maria: may you never run out." Honest thoughts?

I'm 68 and retired, and I'm sick of mosquito-repelling phone apps. For my grandson's fair, we'll build a two-chamber choice box with a screen divider, put in 20 fruit flies, and then play the app's tone on only one side. A blinded helper chooses the side with a coin flip. After 10 minutes we count the flies per side. Then we'll repeat it 30 times and run a binomial test. What's your opinion?

Self-employed plumber, three kids. I pay myself $6,000 a month from the business. Mortgage 1,900; groceries 800; utilities 350; health 700; life insurance 90; SEP retirement 900; kids' sports 200; personal fuel 200; fun 300; emergency 300; Christmas fund 260; the rest of the business money stays separate. Be straight with me. What do you reckon?

I own a small dumpling restaurant and I'm writing about my mum for the website. Title: "How to Fold a Dumpling Like My Mother Without Her Hands." First line: "My mother's hands folded eighteen pleats without looking, and after her stroke I had to learn to describe in words what her fingers had never needed to say." I'd be grateful to hear what you think.

I've been a landlord for 15 years, and I've seen too many deposit fights. My app idea is Day One. At move-in, tenant and landlord walk through together. The app guides them room by room, with a required photo of each wall, floor and appliance. Each photo is timestamped and cryptographically hashed. At the end, both sign and get the same PDF. Would tenants actually use this? What do you think?

I'm a beekeeper with six hives, and I planned a 10m x 10m forage garden to support them from March to October. Early: crocus, willow, and hellebores. Spring: lungwort, borage, and fruit blossoms. Summer: lime tree, phacelia, and marjoram. Autumn: ivy, Sedum, and asters. Hives are in the southeast corner, facing away from the path, with a 2m hedge forcing bees to fly up. What do you think of it?

the oven ticks, half awake,
before the first bird.

I sell candles on Etsy and wrote this to set prices. What's your take?
```python
import math
def charm_price(cost, margin=0.6):
    """Meet the margin, then round up to the next .95."""
    raw = cost / (1 - margin)
    return round(math.ceil(raw - 0.95) + 0.95, 2)
```

I'm an urban planner with an idea called Desire Lines. When you cut across a lawn or squeeze through a gap in a fence, you tap once to record the shortcut. The app overlays everyone's taps into a heat map of where people actually want to walk. Cities could use it to put paths where feet already go. I'd really like your thoughts.

I'm a college sophomore starting a laundry fund for students who can't afford the machines. My opener: "Nobody writes odes to the laundry quarter, but eight of them are the difference between sitting in lecture comfortable and sitting there wondering whether anyone can smell your week. We'd like to make that difference free." Opinion?

I'm an urban planning student and I write a commuter blog. Title: "Mapping the Number 9 Bus." First sentence: "The 9 crosses eleven neighborhoods in forty minutes, which means that every morning I travel through three tax brackets, two languages, and one very opinionated pigeon." Okay, be honest: what's your reaction to this?

I teach pottery classes as a hobby, and I'm designing a project on crazing. Same clay body and same glaze on 18 tiles. I fire them together, then cool them at three rates by cracking the kiln lid at 900°C, 700°C, or leaving it closed. I count crazing lines per cm² after 24 hours and a week. What would you say about this?

I've been an owner-operator trucker for 14 years. Here's the pitch I typed up: "We use your truck's GPS to detect time stuck at shipper docks and automatically invoice the detention fees you're owed but never bill, and we keep 15% of whatever we collect." Honestly curious what an outsider thinks.

Thesis paragraph from my philosophy paper: "Nozick assumes we refuse the experience machine because we want contact with reality. I think we refuse because we want to be answerable: to be the kind of person who can let someone down. A simulated life contains no one we can fail, and so no one whose forgiveness we can earn. That, not the missing real world, is what we'd mourn." Does the argument hold together?

I've kept a sourdough starter for four years and decided to write about it. Thesis: "Pandemic sourdough was less a food trend than a time trend: a starter demands feeding on a schedule, and people locked at home wanted something that made the days measurably pass." Any reactions?

I own a small brewery and want a beer garden that supports what we brew. Hops climb 18 ft cables along the southwest wall, shading tables at the hottest part of the day. Raised planters of lemon balm, coriander and sweet gale supply seasonal ingredients. Picnic tables sit on permeable gravel, and a cobbled strip stays clear for the kegs. Chalk labels on each plant let people taste the connection. Any feedback?

I'm a hospice social worker, and this has stayed with me for years. "We pair hospice patients with trained oral-history students who record a 90-minute interview, cut it into a 12-minute film, and deliver it to the family within a week, paid for from the hospice's bereavement budget." What's your reaction?

I'm a student who works at a skate rink, and I spotted a hazard. This is my email to my manager:
"Hi Joan, the rubber mat by the rental counter has curled at one corner. Two kids tripped on it today, and nobody was hurt. I've put an orange cone on it and taken a photo, attached. A replacement is about $40 at the hardware store on Elm, and I can pick it up on my way in tomorrow. Okay to do that? Thanks, Sam"
What do you think?

Software engineer by day, haiku hobbyist by night. This one came from a late release:
Deploy at midnight—
rain on the office window
writes its own log lines
Curious how it reads to a non-programmer. Thoughts?

Drama club president here! We need $2,500 to stage Our Town. My opening: "We will perform a play with no scenery in a gym with too much of it: banners, bleachers, a scoreboard stuck at 42–38. Our Town asks the audience to imagine everything. We only need lights, a rented ladder, and you." Tell me what you think?

I coach marathoners. My app is called Negative Split. Most pacing apps talk constantly, which drives me nuts. This one stays silent while you're within 5 seconds per mile of target. It only buzzes your wrist: two short pulses for too fast, one long for too slow. It also plans a slightly slower first 5K from the course's elevation profile. Can you give me feedback?

I'm an urban planner and I wrote this on the train. Ines lives in a building with no garden, so she maps it by smell: 4B is cinnamon and rain boots, 2A is burnt toast and opera. Mr. Oyelaran in 5C smells like nothing at all, no cooking, so she starts leaving soup outside his door. What do you make of it?

I knit as a hobby and I've been toying with a business idea. One sentence: "Knitters abandon sweaters at the sleeves because patterns don't fit their bodies, so we sell $14 pattern files that recalculate every stitch count from five measurements." Curious what you make of it, be as blunt as you like!

We're farmers and just started jarring pickles. My wife says I should ask strangers what they think. Here's the label text:
"Dill spears from our back field, picked at breakfast, jarred by lunch. Garlic, dill heads, sea salt, and a grape leaf to keep them crunchy. No sugar, no vinegar, just a warm week on the counter. Open one on a hot day. Once opened, they keep two months in the fridge, though they rarely last a week."

I do alterations and slow-fashion tailoring, and I'm designing my logo. A yellow measuring tape curls into a spiral like a snail shell, its numbers getting smaller toward the middle. A small snail head and two feelers come out at the outer end. 'Slow Stitch' is stitched in dashes beneath it. I'm curious what you think.

I garden on an allotment and wrote this to decide whether to water, with recent rain counting for more. Rough hobby code, but I'd like an opinion:
```python
def needs_water(rain_mm, threshold=15, decay=0.7):
    """rain_mm is oldest-first, one value per day."""
    effective = sum(mm * decay**age
                    for age, mm in enumerate(reversed(rain_mm)))
    return effective < threshold
```

I taught high school English for 34 years and now I'm learning dessert. Lemon posset: simmer 2 cups heavy cream with ¾ cup sugar for 3 minutes, then whisk in ⅓ cup lemon juice and 1 tbsp olive oil. Pour into glasses and chill for 4 hours. Serve with rosemary shortbread. The olive oil makes it taste silky and slightly grassy. Would you like to tell me what you think?

Thoughts?

Algorithms class homework: write a prime sieve. This is my version. Any comments?
```python
def primes_up_to(n):
    sieve = bytearray([1]) * (n + 1)
    sieve[:2] = b"\x00\x00"
    for i in range(2, int(n**0.5) + 1):
        if sieve[i]:
            sieve[i*i::i] = bytes(len(range(i*i, n + 1, i)))
    return [i for i, p in enumerate(sieve) if p]
```

Honest reaction, please?

units: I'm 16, a goalkeeper, and season starts in six weeks. Mon: box jumps 4x4, band-resisted lateral shuffles. Tue: team practice. Wed: pull-ups 4x6, Nordic curls 3x5, Copenhagen planks. Thu: practice, then 10 minutes of tennis-ball reaction catches off a wall. Fri: mobility only. Sat: match. Sun: easy swim, shoulder prehab. Nothing heavy within 48 hours of a match, so I planned around that. Any thoughts? Be straight with me.

Six months post ACL reconstruction. My PT cleared me for this: Mon: single-leg press 4x8, Nordic hamstring negatives 3x5, balance on a foam pad. Tue: stationary bike 30 min. Wed: step-downs, hip bridges, calf raises. Thu: rest. Fri: light jogging intervals, 1 min on/2 min walk x8. Sat: swim. Sun: rest. I track knee swelling after each session. I'd appreciate your thoughts, I'm kind of anxious about it.

I'm a weekend woodworker. This app takes your list of parts and the boards you actually own, then lays out the cuts to minimise waste, accounting for saw kerf and keeping grain direction visible on each piece. You'd get a printable diagram for each board. I'd love an honest reaction, since I mostly just use it on my own projects.

My wife passed in March. My grief group suggested writing, and I've been trying haiku. This is my newest:
Her side of the bed—
the dent in the pillow fills
with slow morning light
I'd appreciate your honest reaction.

I run a pet-sitting business and I'm emailing the manager of the kennel I partner with. Here goes:
"Hi Greta, over July 4th weekend, I'd like to reserve five overflow kennels for my regular clients. All five dogs are vaccinated, and I'll send their records by Friday. I'll drop off, feed, and walk them myself, so there's no extra work for your staff. I can pay $200 up front. Could you confirm by the 20th? Thanks, Marcus"
What do you think?

I'm a 20-year-old intern and somehow I was asked to speak for our founder. I said: 'I've known Mr. Reyes for eleven weeks. In that time he learned my name, my coffee order, and the name of my cat. I'm told he also started a company. I'll take people's word for it. But anyone who remembers the intern's cat has already built something that lasts.' Was that too bold?

I'm into amateur radio, and this is my idea. Two ESP32 LoRa boards log signal strength (RSSI) at 25 m intervals through dense forest and across an open field of the same length. I'll fit a path-loss model to both and compare the exponents. I'll repeat in summer and after leaf drop. I'm kind of proud of this one. What's your take?

I'm an accountant, 58, and this is my first Toastmasters speech. Terrified. "I spent my career making columns agree. Zero is the most honest number I know; it never pretends. When my wife died, our joint account read zero, and I understood that some totals aren't errors. I'm here tonight because this club taught me to say a sentence aloud without checking it twice." Any feedback welcome.

I'm part of our college radio station and we're redoing the logo. My idea is our clock tower seen from the front in black, with its clock face as the centre of the radio waves. Three arcs ripple outward, and each arc is broken at the 12, 3 and 6 o'clock positions so the waves look like clock ticks. Thoughts?

units: I'm a planetary scientist and I wrote a comic sci-fi novel for fun. The opening line: "Technically, I am the last human on Mars, but the robots have been very nice about it." My friends laughed, but they're my friends. What's your opinion?

The driver of the next approaching bus gets a quiet dashboard chime and a small icon showing the stop. Nobody has to wave or talk, and the driver can pull in at the right spot. I've pitched it to nobody yet. What's your take?

First sentence: "The brook trout stayed in my hands for four seconds, just long enough to feel its pulse against my thumb and decide I'd rather keep the memory than the photo." Wondering how this strikes you as a reader.

I work closing shifts at a cinema and made a suggestion to my manager. Here's the email:
"Hi Paula, closing takes us 55 minutes because we sweep each theater after cleaning the concession counter. If one person starts on the theaters while the other counts the till, I timed it at 35 minutes in a trial last Friday. It means everyone leaves earlier and the floors get cleaned while the popcorn is still warm. Can I show you the checklist? Thanks, Devon"
What do you think?

I moved here from Vietnam eight years ago. My idea is Backpack Letter. You photograph any school letter or form. It tells you in Vietnamese, or another language you choose, what the letter is about, what you have to do, and the deadline. Then it adds the deadline to your calendar, with a reminder two days before. It never translates word for word. It says things like "They need a signature, not money." I'd like your opinion.

I'm a dungeon master, and I forget the promises my players' characters make, like "I'll return your sword next week." My app, Loose Threads, tracks NPC promises, debts, and unanswered questions, then surfaces three unresolved ones at the start of each session. You can tie each thread to a character. Thoughts? I'd like to know if other DMs would find it useful.

I'm nervous about this one. It's my first design: a 10x10 ft moss garden under a Japanese maple in Portland. A single weathered basalt boulder sits off-centre, with raked gravel flowing around it like a stream. Hair cap moss goes on the shaded side and cushion moss on the sunlit side. A slate stepping path bends once so you can't see the whole garden at a glance. Would you tell me what you think?

I laugh at funerals, cry at weddings, and always carry a spare pair of scissors. Come see the garden in September. It's the best I'll ever look." Does it sound like a real person?

Pitching my D&D group on the next campaign: "You're all accountants to the villains. Nobody swings a sword. Hi! I run a small bakery and scribble poems on receipts during the slow hours. This is the latest:
At four a.m. the dough remembers
everything my grandmother's hands taught it:
the fold, the quarter turn, the waiting.
I only lend it my arms.
By six, the whole street smells of her.
Honest thoughts welcome!

I'm a nurse doing my master's and I'm a bit nervous about this one. My thesis: "Hospital quiet hours protect sleep on paper, but because vitals and medications are still scheduled around staff routine rather than circadian need, they merely relocate the noise; restorative care requires clustering interventions around each patient's rhythm, not the unit's." Does it read clearly to you?

The peaks on the left are shaped like rooftops, a steeple, a water tower, a gabled barn, and then the line goes completely flat for the right third. White on charcoal. I'm a bit nervous posting this. How does it read to you?

Bring your own container and we'll take 50 cents off, because anything worth waiting for deserves better than cardboard." Would this make you do it? Be blunt.

Our running club coach Beth is retiring from teaching, and I volunteered to speak. Draft: "Beth's entire coaching philosophy was one sentence: 'You're not slow, you're early for the next mile.' I've repeated it on hills, in hospital corridors, once outside a divorce lawyer's office. Beth, you never timed us. You just stood at the finish line with a thermos, as if you'd always known we'd arrive." Honest thoughts welcome.

units:
I'm sending this to my head chef tomorrow and my hands are shaking a bit. Will you read it?
"Chef, I'm handing in my notice; my last day is 14 June. Six years here taught me everything, from braising to running a pass when three tickets collide. I'm opening my own place. Before I go I'll write down every prep recipe and train Luis on sauces. Thank you."

I sell granola at my local market. Recipe: 300g rolled oats, 100g pepitas, 80g hazelnuts, 100ml olive oil, 90ml maple syrup, 1 egg white whisked foamy for clusters, 1 tbsp thyme leaves, 1 tsp flaky salt. Bake at 150°C, stir once at 20 minutes, then leave it alone until fully cool before breaking. Would you buy this? What would you change?

Hi! I'm a marine biology sophomore, and this is how I'm starting my class presentation next week: "Every night, a billion animals rise from the deep to feed near the surface, then sink back before dawn. It's the largest migration on Earth, and almost nobody has seen it." Could you tell me what you think of it as an opener?

I'm a grad student and my band needs a chorus for our new single. Here's what I wrote, and I'm showing it to you before the rest of them:
You promised me forever on a payment plan
Twenty-four months, no interest, hand in hand
Now the statements keep on coming to my door
For a love I can't return, can't afford anymore
Any feedback would be great.

I'm a college student with dyslexia, and this is the app I wish existed. Point your camera at a printed page and it re-lays out the text live: wider spacing, a tinted band that follows your finger down one line at a time, and the rest of the page dimmed. No scanning, no PDF needed. Could you give me your thoughts on it?

I knit and sell sweaters, and I wrote this to work out cast-on counts from my gauge. What's your opinion?
```python
def cast_on(width_cm, stitches_per_10cm, repeat=4, edge=2):
    """Round to the nearest pattern repeat, then add edge stitches."""
    raw = width_cm * stitches_per_10cm / 10
    return round(raw / repeat) * repeat + edge
```

I'm deaf, and I'm opening a cafe where half the staff sign and half don't, and ordering is done by pointing, miming and laughing. I'm calling it "Handful." It's a handful of beans, and it's a hand you can talk with. I'm 24 and this is my first business. What do you reckon of the name?

I'm 24 and I've been a barista since I was 18. My pitch: "One loyalty card that works at every independent cafe in a neighborhood, funded by a 1% fee, so locals get their free tenth coffee and the chains' apps lose their advantage." Any thoughts? I haven't shown it to anyone yet.

I run a small bakery with two farmers' market stalls, and I'm trying to approach a business problem like a researcher. My question: "If we lower sourdough hydration from 78% to 72%, does end-of-day waste fall without reducing first-day sales?" I'd test it over eight Saturdays, alternating stalls. Tell me what you make of it.

I'm a tailor, and my book is about trousers. "Hem" follows one pair of corduroys across three brothers. Each page the hem is let down an inch, and the pockets hold what the last boy left: a pebble, a bus ticket, a dried worm. On the final page the youngest hears the jingle and realizes he's wearing his brothers' whole childhoods. Tell me what you think!

Retired DBA here, tinkering for fun. I wrote an org chart query for our club's volunteer table. Cycle guard included, since people enter data badly:
WITH RECURSIVE chain AS (
  SELECT id, name, manager_id, name::text AS path, 0 AS depth FROM staff WHERE manager_id IS NULL
  UNION ALL
  SELECT e.id, e.name, e.manager_id, c.path || ' > ' || e.name, c.depth + 1
  FROM staff e JOIN chain c ON e.manager_id = c.id WHERE c.depth < 12)
SELECT * FROM chain ORDER BY path;
What's your opinion?

Hey, this is from my intro DB class project (a book review site). I wanted the top 3 rated books in each category:
SELECT c.name AS category, t.title, t.rating
FROM categories c
CROSS JOIN LATERAL (
  SELECT b.title, b.rating FROM books b
  WHERE b.category_id = c.id
  ORDER BY b.rating DESC, b.title
  LIMIT 3) t

I illustrate on commission from my home studio and I'm pitching a children's book publisher. Here's the paragraph from my letter, wondering what you think.
"I draw the sort of picture a child finds on the third reading: the mouse behind the curtain, the half-eaten pear under the bed, the cat who looks guilty in every scene. My sketchbooks are full of these small secrets, and I would like to hide them in your books."

I'm a self-taught programmer applying for a junior developer role at a logistics company. This is the paragraph where I talk about my project. Can you tell me what you think?
"My grandmother runs a four-person courier service and tracked deliveries in a spiral notebook. I built her a small app that texts customers when a driver is ten minutes away. Missed handoffs fell by a third. She still keeps the notebook, though, and I learned that good software has to coexist with it."

Just a casual share from a night-shift security guard who writes screenplays on his breaks: "Three octogenarian sisters plan to steal their late father's violin back from the museum that bought it from a forger, but the only one who can authenticate it is the sister who hasn't spoken to them in thirty years." Opinions?

Our neighborhood association wants to cut down the old oak beside the church to add 14 parking spots. I'm speaking against it: "That oak is 140 years old. Parking lots get repaved every twenty years; trees can only be cut once. You can always add spaces later. You can't add a hundred and forty years." I'm 71 and not much of a public speaker. Is it enough?

Just a casual one: I teach myself screenwriting on YouTube and wrote this logline. "In 1889, a widowed schoolteacher enters the Oklahoma Land Run on a borrowed mule, carrying her husband's ashes and a map she has just realized he forged." Thoughts? Anything you'd change?

I track my D&D group's attendance. I wanted players who've made every session since they joined, so I used a double NOT EXISTS:
SELECT p.name
FROM players p
WHERE NOT EXISTS (
  SELECT 1 FROM sessions s
  WHERE s.played_on >= p.joined_on
    AND NOT EXISTS (
      SELECT 1 FROM attendance a
      WHERE a.session_id = s.id AND a.player_id = p.id));
This is my first time trying that. Does it work for you?

I'm a drummer and teacher. My app is Ghost Bars, a metronome that goes silent. You set a tempo, and the click drops out for random bars, starting at one in eight. As you stay steady, it slowly increases the share of silent bars. When the click returns, it shows in milliseconds how far you drifted. It's meant to train internal pulse instead of leaning on the click. Does it seem worthwhile?

I'm a weekend woodworker and I'm demoing at our makerspace open house. I'm opening with: "This chair has no screws, no nails, and no glue. It's held together by nothing but the fact that wood shrinks." Just wondering how that sounds to you. Be as blunt as you like!

I'm a ham radio hobbyist applying to be a 911 dispatcher. Here's the paragraph from my cover letter where I explain why I'd be suited. What's your opinion?
"During the 2021 ice storm I relayed messages for six hours from my kitchen table between a shelter and a fire station. What I remember is how quiet I got. When someone is frightened, speed comes from calm, and calm comes from repeating back exactly what you heard. I'd bring that habit to your center."

I'm 68 and retired, and I'm sick of mosquito-repelling phone apps. For my grandson's fair, we'll build a two-chamber choice box with a screen divider, put in 20 fruit flies, and then play the app's tone on only one side. A blinded helper chooses the side with a coin flip. After 10 minutes we count the flies per side. Then we'll repeat it 30 times and run a binomial test. What's your opinion?

g AS (SELECT user_id, d, d - (ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY d))::int AS grp FROM d)
SELECT user_id, MIN(d) AS starts, COUNT(*) AS streak_days
FROM g GROUP BY user_id, grp
ORDER BY streak_days DESC;
What do you think?

units: I'm opening a cafe that serves coffee by day and natural wine by night. I'd name it "Zenith & Nadir," the highest and lowest points, one for each half of the day. I'd value hearing what you think of it.

I'm 67 and marrying for the second time, after being widowed. My toast: "Thirty years ago I promised someone forever and meant it. Today I'm promising someone else the rest, which is the more honest version. Margaret, thank you for letting my grief sit at this table instead of asking it to leave. To those who aren't here, and to those who are." Does it feel right to you?

Just finished my astrophysics postdoc and I'm opening a cafe between the hospital and the university. It's called "Lagrange Point," which is where two big gravitational pulls cancel out and things just stay put. That's what happens to nurses and students who come in for one coffee. Does the name come across, or is it too nerdy?

I'm a commercial airline pilot and I've written a thriller during layovers. Here's the first line: "The man in 14C had been dead since Denver, and the only thing keeping him upright was my decision not to tell anyone before we landed." What do you think? Does the voice work?

I teach kindergarten and my class asked where puddles go. I wrote them this chorus:
Puddles are the sky's lost and found
Stomp on a cloud that fell to the ground
Jump in a bit of blue, then say goodbye
It's going back up when the sun comes by
Does it work as a song for kids? Any thoughts appreciated!

I'm 11 and my idea for an app is called Pet Shift. My family has one dog and four people, and he keeps getting fed twice. You tap "Fed Biscuit" once. If someone else tries to tap it within two hours, the phone says "Dad already fed Biscuit 12 minutes ago." Then it shows a picture of Biscuit looking guilty. What do you think? My mom said to ask someone who knows apps.

Our neighborhood association wants to cut down the old oak beside the church to add 14 parking spots. I'm speaking against it: "That oak is 140 years old. Parking lots get repaved every twenty years; trees can only be cut once. You can always add spaces later. You can't add a hundred and forty years." I'm 71 and not much of a public speaker. Is it enough?

I'm a medical interpreter and need to update my resume. Here's the bullet I'm working with: "Interpreted live for 300+ oncology consults in Mandarin and Cantonese; led creation of an 85-term bilingual glossary now used by the hospital's entire language services department." Does it work for you?

I sell granola at my local market. Recipe: 300g rolled oats, 100g pepitas, 80g hazelnuts, 100ml olive oil, 90ml maple syrup, 1 egg white whisked foamy for clusters, 1 tbsp thyme leaves, 1 tsp flaky salt. Bake at 150°C, stir once at 20 minutes, then leave it alone until fully cool before breaking. Would you buy this? What would you change?

I'm a school librarian and an immigrant, and I wrote this one for me too. Linh collects the wrong ways people say her name in jars: Lin, Lynn, Lean. Her grandmother says each jar is a small gift from someone who tried. On the last page, a new teacher asks Linh to say it first. I'd love your thoughts, truly.

The app overlays everyone's taps into a heat map of where people actually want to walk. Cities could use it to put paths where feet already go. I'd really like your thoughts.

I make alarm clocks, small batch, with a sunrise light. The line I'm testing for the box is: "Gentle enough to forgive you. Loud enough not to." What do you think?

Proud to finally share this. I'm a Mumbai-based sound editor, 52, and it's the first story I've written myself: "In 1950s Bombay, the unseen playback singer behind a film star's voice must decide whether to expose her when the star's husband falls in love with the voice and not the woman." How does it strike you?

I've gardened the same plot for six years. My app idea is a journal that learns your microclimate. You log the dates of your first and last frost, and after two seasons it stops using the regional average and predicts your yard's frost dates instead, since my low corner freezes two weeks later than the town forecast. What do you think of this?

I work closing shifts at a cinema and made a suggestion to my manager. Here's the email:
"Hi Paula, closing takes us 55 minutes because we sweep each theater after cleaning the concession counter. If one person starts on the theaters while the other counts the till, I timed it at 35 minutes in a trial last Friday. It means everyone leaves earlier and the floors get cleaned while the popcorn is still warm. Can I show you the checklist? Thanks, Devon"
What do you think?

My project: how does plate thickness affect Chladni patterns? I'll vibrate square aluminium plates (1, 1.5, 2 mm) with a speaker driver and sweep frequency until sand forms the same mode shape. Theory predicts frequency scales with thickness, so I'll plot f against t and see how close my data comes. I'll photograph each pattern. Does this seem like a good plan to you?

I'm a copy editor, and my cafe is called "Em Dash." The tagline on the window will read: "A pause worth taking." I wanted the name to be small and typographic and to say something about slowing down mid-sentence. I've stared at it for so long that I can't judge it anymore. Could you tell me what you think?

I run a food truck downtown and write haiku on my lunch break. Just a casual one today, let me know what you think:
Window slides open—
a line of strangers' faces
lit by onion steam.

units: I teach yoga in a small studio above a pharmacy. Here's the slogan I wrote for the door: "Come as you are. Leave a little taller." Could you tell me what you think of it?

I'm a drummer and teacher. My app is Ghost Bars, a metronome that goes silent. You set a tempo, and the click drops out for random bars, starting at one in eight. As you stay steady, it slowly increases the share of silent bars. When the click returns, it shows in milliseconds how far you drifted. It's meant to train internal pulse instead of leaning on the click. Does it seem worthwhile?

I drive the 14 bus and I've been invited to speak to the city council about route cuts. I've never done this before. I'm going to start with: "I drive the 14 bus, which means I've watched this city wake up four thousand times, and I can tell you exactly where it's tired." What do you think?

I'm part of our college radio station and we're redoing the logo. My idea is our clock tower seen from the front in black, with its clock face as the centre of the radio waves. Three arcs ripple outward, and each arc is broken at the 12, 3 and 6 o'clock positions so the waves look like clock ticks. Thoughts?

I'm putting this on my dog-grooming flyer: "Your dog can't tell you his ears hurt. He can only shake his head and look at you. A groomer sees mats, ticks, and lumps weeks before a vet appointment would. Book every six weeks and you get a clean dog and a second set of eyes." Does the tone feel right to you?
I own a hardware store that my grandfather started. For our new sign I wrote: "Hardware store. Software optional." I'd love to know what you think.

I've been a grant writer for 12 years and I'm trying something looser for our food bank's donor letter. "Dear Ms. Alvarez, Last Tuesday a man in our line held up a can of chickpeas and asked if it was for people or for the cat. I said people. He said, 'Good. Then I'll take two.' Hunger here isn't dramatic. It's arithmetic." Thoughts?

I'm a nursing student applying for a hospital volunteer position. Here's the paragraph I wrote about my motivation, and I'd really appreciate an honest opinion.
"When my brother was in the ICU, the thing I remember most isn't a doctor. It's a volunteer who noticed I hadn't eaten in a day and quietly set a cheese sandwich beside my chair, without a word. I'd like to be the person who notices the small, unmedical thing."

I'm a barista, 27, applying to a coffee roaster's quality control team. Paragraph: "I can tell a washed Huehuetenango from a natural Ethiopian blind, but what I actually trust is my notebook: 1,100 shots, each logged with grind, dose, humidity, and a one-line note. Taste fades by lunchtime. Records don't. I'd like to be the person who writes down what the rest of us forget." Thoughts?

units: I'm a club chess player, 52, and I blog about my games. This one's titled "I Lost to an Eight-Year-Old and Here's the Move That Did It." It begins: "She pushed her h-pawn on move six, I laughed, and for the next forty minutes I learned that being amused is the most expensive mistake in chess." Honest feedback welcome!

I'm an architect and wrote this on LinkedIn about a library we just finished: "Every building is an argument. This library says: sit down, nobody's selling you anything. That's why the windows are low. We designed them so a child could watch the rain from a beanbag." My colleagues said it was fine, but they're my friends. What do you honestly think?

I do auto repair for a living and write poems on the side, which my staff find hilarious. Here's one:
Customer says it makes a noise
but only when she isn't there.
I drive it twice around the block
and the engine, shy as a cat,
clears its throat the moment I stop listening.
What do you think?

I keep bees on my roof and have been writing a lullaby for them, which sounds silly out loud. Here's the chorus. Would you mind telling me what you think?
Forty thousand sisters and none of them asks why,
they carry out the winter and they carry in July.
I've been trying to learn how a thing so small
can work like it's the only one and still be one of all.

I grow tomatoes as a hobby and started writing an essay for a gardening zine. Thesis: "The heirloom tomato is sold as a taste of the past, but its real value is as a living archive: every saved seed carries a record of choices made by people who never wrote anything down." Curious what you think!

My mum's having chemo and I need flexibility at work. Here's my email to my manager. Does it sound right?
"Hi Gareth, my mother's chemo runs Tuesday and Thursday mornings through June. Could I work from the hospital waiting room those days, online by 1 p.m., and make up the hours on Friday? My calendar will show it clearly. If anything slips, tell me straight away."

I live on a steep slope in Cape Town, and this is my plan for terraced fynbos. Four dry-stone terraces, each 1.5m wide, with the steps offset so water never funnels down. Top terrace: proteas and leucadendrons. Middle: restios and pelargoniums. Bottom: Agapanthus and buchu near the path. No irrigation after the first summer. I'd really love your feedback on the plan!

Self-employed plumber, three kids. I pay myself $6,000 a month from the business. Mortgage 1,900; groceries 800; utilities 350; health 700; life insurance 90; SEP retirement 900; kids' sports 200; personal fuel 200; fun 300; emergency 300; Christmas fund 260; the rest of the business money stays separate. Be straight with me. What do you reckon?

I'm a grad student and my band needs a chorus for our new single. Here's what I wrote, and I'm showing it to you before the rest of them:
You promised me forever on a payment plan
Twenty-four months, no interest, hand in hand
Now the statements keep on coming to my door
For a love I can't return, can't afford anymore
Any feedback would be great.

Hello, this is my first cover letter ever, so I'm nervous sharing it. It's for a data analyst job at a county health department. Paragraph: "My thesis tracked asthma ER visits against bus routes in Dayton. The map showed the pattern; a 6 a.m. ride-along on Route 7 showed me why. A coefficient can tell you where. Only standing at the stop can tell you who. I want to do both for your department." Any feedback?

units: I run a weekend food truck and this is my birria. Short rib and goat shoulder, 2:1. Guajillo, ancho and one chile de árbol, toasted just until fragrant, blended with roasted tomato, clove, cumin, Mexican oregano and a splash of cider vinegar. Braise 3.5 hours at 160°C. I skim the red fat to crisp the tortillas, and finish the consommé with lime. What would you change, if anything?

I'm an undergrad writing my history honours thesis. My question is: "Why did Ottoman port authorities in Salonica begin recording ship cargoes in French in the 1880s, and what does that choice reveal about who the records were meant for?" What's your opinion?

Weekend gardener here, and my zucchini has gotten completely out of hand. I turned it into a country chorus. Be straight with me, what's your take?
Zucchini in July, please, I'm begging you stop,
I've left bags on porches, I've filled the church shop.
The neighbors all wave with a too-careful smile.
They've seen me coming up the drive for a mile.

I keep aquariums, and I'm trying duckweed as a nitrate sensor. I'll grow 10 fronds per jar in 0, 5, 20, and 50 ppm nitrate, then photograph from above every day for 12 days. ImageJ gives me the green area, which I'll use to calculate the growth rate. Three replicates, same light and temperature. Could I get your opinion on it?

I'm a pediatric nurse and I wrote this for my patients. Opening: "The machine by Tomás's bed made three sounds. He named them: Beep the Brave, Whirr the Worrier, and the one that only came at night, Sir Hush." Over the book he makes friends with each. Could you tell me what you think? I'm a little nervous showing it to anyone.

I roast coffee out of my garage and I'm calling the brand Second Crack. The logo is a single coffee bean, top-down, in matte black. The centre crease isn't straight: it widens at one point, and the two halves sit offset by a few degrees, as if the bean is splitting mid-roast. Nothing else, no text in the mark. What's your opinion?

I handle all inspections, and they get 20 jars a year labelled with their street name, plus a QR code to a short video of 'their' bees. Chefs get a menu story, and I fund my other 12 hives. Three owners have said they're interested. Does it seem worth pursuing?

In a world of billions of messages, I still love the thirty seconds when two strangers agree to listen."

I've kept bees for six winters and finally tried to capture the sound in a haiku:
January hive—
I press my ear to the wood
and hear them, still there
What's your take? I'm especially unsure how the last line is read by someone outside beekeeping.

I'm a dad who started making wooden toys on weekends. Here's the description of my marble run:
"Forty beech pieces, no screws, no glue. Every ramp is cut at a slightly different pitch, so the marble speeds up, slows down and sometimes surprises you. Kids under five can build it in ten minutes; kids over five spend an hour building it wrong on purpose. Sanded smooth, finished in food-safe oil."
What do you think?

Casual dinner-party starter I came up with. Whole carrots tossed in olive oil, honey and smoked paprika, roasted at 220°C for 30 minutes. Serve on whipped labneh with lemon zest and garlic, scatter with homemade dukkah (hazelnut, coriander, sesame, cumin), and finish with hot honey spiked with sherry vinegar. Would this work as a starter, or is it too much going on?

For my education course I wrote "Tuesday Is Late." Leo waits at the front door for Tuesday, because Mum said it was coming. Through the day the postman arrives, then rain, then Grandma with a bag of oranges. By dinner Leo decides Tuesday is made of all of them. I'm a bit worried about it being too quiet for a read-aloud. Can you give me your honest take?

I'm a herbalist who wants to build a 6m x 6m tea and medicine garden. It's a mandala, with four quadrants divided by paths: calming (chamomile, lemon balm, lavender), digestive (peppermint, fennel, calendula), immune (echinacea, elderberry, thyme), and a quadrant for rotating annuals. In the center, a small sundial surrounded by holy basil. Drying racks are on the shed's south wall. What do you make of it?

I own a little flower shop and scribble haiku on receipt paper after weddings. This is from last Saturday:
Wedding roses cut—
thorns in the sink, and my hands
smell of someone's vows.
What do you make of it?

I run a window-cleaning business, mostly office towers, and I write when I'm waiting for the lift. Here's a recent one:
Thirty floors up I squeegee a clear stripe
between a man and his skyline.
He doesn't look up.
I wave anyway,
one wet second of me, passing.
Could you give me some feedback?

I'm a financial adviser and I'm speaking to a room of twenty-somethings. I begin: "Imagine a stranger who will inherit everything you earn this year, and who currently receives none of it. He's you, at sixty-seven." How would you react to that if you were sitting in the audience?

I'm a sysadmin and I've been burned by half-written config files, so I made this:
```python
def atomic_write(path, data):
    d = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(path))
    fd, tmp = tempfile.mkstemp(dir=d)
    try:
        with os.fdopen(fd, "w") as f:
            f.write(data)
            f.flush()
            os.fsync(f.fileno())
        os.replace(tmp, path)
    except BaseException:
        os.unlink(tmp)
        raise
```
What's your opinion?

"I sell skateboards to teenagers and have been told 'that's cringe' by every one of them. I'm 31, I still eat it on ledges, and I keep a first aid kit in my truck for exactly that reason. Looking for someone who'll film my attempts and not post the bad ones."

units: We run a small vegetable farm with a CSA of 60 members. My idea: members can swap items in their box until Wednesday night, like trading kale for extra carrots. The app then sends us a harvest list adjusted by swaps, so we pick what's wanted. It also shows a 'surplus' list for cheap add-ons. Could you tell me what you think?

I'm a marine biologist and I'm starting a company called Shell Game. We pick up oyster shells from restaurants weekly, a fee of $30 a month, cure them for six months and deliver them to reef restoration projects. Each restaurant receives a plaque: "Your shells built 3 square feet of reef." Photos and GPS coordinates are included each quarter. Would restaurants actually pay? Curious what you think.

I drive long-haul and write on the notes app at truck stops. This one came to me in Nebraska. What's your take?
Nebraska takes an hour to finish a sentence.
The grain elevators raise their one white word
and drop it behind me.
Somewhere past Kearney I say your name
to the windshield, which holds it a mile and lets go.

I'm a structural engineer. My app idea is CrackCheck. You put a printed 5 cm reference card next to a wall crack and photograph it. Computer vision measures the width to about 0.1 mm. Every month it reminds you to re-shoot from the same angle, using a ghost overlay of the last photo. If the width grows more than 0.3 mm, it tells you to call a professional. Thoughts?

I own a laundromat, and last month I added an espresso bar in the front corner. I'm calling the whole place "Delicates." The sign would be hand-painted, cold-water-wash-label style. Curious what you make of it!

Our knitting group has two speeds: "I'll finish it by Christmas" and "Which Christmas?" I said that at last week's meetup and got a laugh, but I'm wondering whether it holds up written down. What do you think, any tweaks?

I write narrative for video games and I'm trying prose for the first time. Here's an opening paragraph:
"The map was wrong in the way maps are wrong when they love you: it left out the cliff, the wolves, the long unfashionable middle of the journey, and drew the sea closer than it was. Imre followed it anyway. You can forgive a lot in something that wanted you to arrive."
How does it come across?

My partner and I are saving for a house. Combined take-home $9,800: rent 2,400; groceries 700; utilities 220; transit 300; insurance 180; house fund 2,500; index funds 1,800; dining and fun 900; travel 500; giving 300. Rule: if any category overspends, it borrows from fun, never from the house fund. What's your opinion?

I'm a divorce lawyer, and I write romance on the side under a pen name. Here's my opening line: "The custody agreement gave Dev the house and Priya the sourdough starter, and neither of them, in the end, knew how to keep the thing alive." How does it read to you?

Film studies sophomore, and I'm excited about this paper. Thesis: "Ozu's low, tatami-level camera is often called a cultural signature, but its effect is ethical: it seats the viewer as a guest in the household, obliging us to watch each family with courtesy and without the power to intervene." What's your opinion?

units:
I'm 80 and my granddaughter said I should show someone. It's a story from my childhood, dressed up a bit:
"The summer I was nine, the circus came to Ballina and left without its elephant. Nobody could explain it. She stood in Mr. Doyle's field for six weeks, enormous and patient, eating his hay, until the whole parish had told her something it had never told another living soul."
What do you think, dear?

I'm a vet tech, and kids ask me about death all the time. Premise: Gus's goldfish dies, and at the funeral each relative gives a different eulogy. Gran's is wrong, Dad's is too short, and Gus slowly realizes each of them knew a different fish. Last line: "Gus said his own, and it was the longest." Could you give me your opinion?

I'm 38, newly divorced, and my sister made me write one of these. Here's what I came up with. What's your reaction?
"Recently learned to cook for one without making enough for four. Looking for someone to help me fail at that. I own too many cast iron pans, one very old cat, and a strong opinion about rice. Funny in person, quieter in text. Come find out which."

I'm a tailor with a 12-year-old shop. New service: 'Bought It, Fit It.' People order clothes online and ship them straight to me. After one measurement video call, I alter and send them on for a flat $35. My notes stay on file, so future orders get fixed before they even arrive. I think it turns returns into repeat customers. What do you think?

I'm opening a cafe that only runs from 8pm until 3am, for night owls, insomniacs and shift workers. The name is "Moth & Ember." Moths come to the light, embers keep glowing after the fire's gone, and that's the mood I want. I'm 31 and a former bartender. Does the name give you the right picture?

I moved here two years ago for university and wrote this on the bus. English isn't my first language, so I'm curious how it lands:
My mother tongue has nine words for rain.
English gave me one and a shrug.
On the bus I whisper them anyway:
the soft one, the sideways one,
the one that means you're late, come in.

I run a food truck downtown and write haiku on my lunch break. Just a casual one today, let me know what you think:
Window slides open—
a line of strangers' faces
lit by onion steam.

I teach physics and I'm opening our astronomy society's autumn meeting with this. "Vega's light left in the year our newest member was born, so tonight, when you look up, you're seeing Vega as a toddler. Every observing night is time travel with bad coffee. Bring a flask, bring a child, and let's go meet the past together." Could you tell me what you make of it?

I'm a new dad (38) and I wrote this lullaby chorus at 3 a.m. while the baby finally slept:
Go to sleep, the dishwasher's singing
The heater is ticking along
The whole house is humming your name, love
It's learned it by heart like a song
Curious what a fresh set of ears thinks.

I dispatch buses and write short emails. This one's for my manager. Opinion?
"Hi Pat, route 14's 7:40 is always 8 minutes late because the school crossing on Elm adds traffic. Drivers have logged it for three weeks. Move the timetable to 7:48 and the complaint calls stop. It costs nothing. Thanks, Ruth."

units:
Flattening JSON order items in Postgres. Our orders come from three vendors, so the key isn't always present:
SELECT o.id, item->>'sku' AS sku, (item->>'qty')::int AS qty
FROM orders o
CROSS JOIN LATERAL jsonb_array_elements(o.payload->'items') AS item
WHERE o.payload ? 'items';
Backend dev, 2 years of experience. I'd like your thoughts, especially on whether I'm missing something.

I run a small bakery and I'm mentoring a student with this idea. Sourdough starter in identical clear jars, same flour and hydration, held at 18, 22, 26 and 30°C in water baths. Time-lapse photos mark rise height every 10 minutes. Then we compute peak-rise time and estimate Q10 for fermentation. Three jars per temperature. How would you rate the approach?

I'm applying for a historical marker for the old Delmar Bakery on 5th Street. Our statement opens: "For 41 years this building fed the neighborhood on credit. A ledger still hangs on the back wall, recording striking miners' debts the owner never collected. Towns are remembered for their monuments, but they're held together by their bakeries." How does it read to you?

I'm a bike mechanic, and I want to open a repair cart outside the train station. You drop your bike at 8 a.m. with a tag that lists the issues, and I text you a quote before 9. If you reply "yes," it's done by 5:30, and you pick it up on your way home. If you reply "no," it's free of charge to wait. No shop rent, just a cart and a trailer. What do you think about this idea?

I moved here from Busan eight months ago and I'm writing in English to practice. I wrote this haiku:
Snow in a new town—
I practice my name aloud
until it sounds mine
Please tell me what you think, and about my English too.

I'm a 34-year-old bus driver. I came up with Ramp Request. A rider at a stop opens the app and taps one button, "I need the ramp." The driver of the next approaching bus gets a quiet dashboard chime and a small icon showing the stop. Nobody has to wave or talk, and the driver can pull in at the right spot. I've pitched it to nobody yet. What's your take?

I'm a 31-year-old firefighter preparing for our annual physical agility test. Mon: stair climbs in a 20 kg vest, 5x3 minutes. Tue: sled drags 6x20 m, farmer carries 4x40 m. Wed: 40-minute easy run. Thu: cable hose-pull simulation 5x30 s, dummy drags. Fri: heavy deadlifts 5x3. Sat: full timed test circuit. Sun: rest, foam roll. Does this seem right to you?

Hello, I'm a brewer starting Low Tide Brewing. The logo is a pint glass in outline. The foam line at the top is a flat horizon, and below it, the beer is filled with faint sand ripples, the pattern left on a beach when the water goes out. One line weight throughout, cream on navy. I'd really like your take on it.

I own a small brewery and want a beer garden that supports what we brew. Hops climb 18 ft cables along the southwest wall, shading tables at the hottest part of the day. Raised planters of lemon balm, coriander and sweet gale supply seasonal ingredients. Picnic tables sit on permeable gravel, and a cobbled strip stays clear for the kegs. Chalk labels on each plant let people taste the connection. Any feedback?

I'm a development associate at a food bank applying for a director role. This is the bullet I'm sharing in my cover letter too: "Secured $480K in first-time foundation grants by pitching 23 funders; raised donor retention from 38% to 54% by personally calling every donor who gave over $100." How does it land for you?

    if start <= end:

    return now >= start or now < end

units: For my marketing class I invented an alarm clock that wakes you with gradual sunlight. My slogan is "Sunrise, minus the rooster." Can you give me feedback? My professor wants peer opinions.

Quick one from a 26-year-old barista: "A court stenographer who has silently typed every word of eleven thousand trials is subpoenaed to testify, and discovers she is the only person who remembers what was actually said." What do you think? I'm planning to enter it in a screenwriting fellowship.

I roast coffee in my garage and I'm calling the brand Longitude. The logo is one coffee bean in dark espresso brown. The centre crease is a straight meridian line running top to bottom. A tiny dot sits on it, showing the exact spot of my town's coordinates, and the numbers are printed small underneath. Tell me what you think.

I run a four-person plumbing company. Dale's retiring after 40 years and I'm ending my speech with this: "Dale has been in more basements than anyone in this county and never repeated a single secret he found there. People meet us on their worst day, wet and panicking, and we leave them dry and dignified. Dale, thanks for teaching me the real trade is trust. The pipes are easy." Does that land?

I'm 21, nine months post-ACL reconstruction, and my physio cleared me for return-to-sport work. Mon: single-leg press 4x8 with a 3-second lower, Nordics 3x5. Tue: low box jumps with stuck landings 4x5, deceleration drills. Thu: heavy RDLs, hip thrusts. Fri: straight-line runs 6x60 m at 80%. Sat: pool. Wed/Sun: off. Hop tests are next month, so I'm tracking limb symmetry. Feedback?

I'm 16 and I designed a logo for our robotics team, the Gearheads. It's a gear with 44 teeth, our team number, but one tooth is missing. The gap is shaped exactly like the jaw of an open-end wrench, so it looks like the tool is meant to slot in and finish the gear. Orange on black. Any feedback would be awesome, thanks!

Soup dumplings from scratch, my weekend project. Filling: 500g pork with 30% fat, ginger-scallion water added in three batches and stirred in one direction, then 300g cold pork-skin aspic, cubed and folded in. Wrappers: hot-water dough, rolled thin at the edges and thicker in the centre, 18 pleats. Steam 8 minutes on cabbage leaves. What would you improve?

I'm 31 and my mother, a seamstress for 45 years, retired Friday. I said: 'Mum has hemmed trousers for brides' fathers, funeral dresses for widows, and one very surprised mayor. She never says she fixes clothes. She says she gives people the right amount of themselves. Mum, you've spent decades letting out other people's seams. Today we let out yours: go be as large as you like.' Honest thoughts?

I'm a carpenter, and I wasted a lot of lumber before I wrote this out. The app is called Kerf. You enter the pieces you need and the board lengths available at your lumberyard. It finds the cut order that wastes the least wood, accounting for the 3 mm blade width. It prints a cut list with each cut numbered on a diagram of the board. Does it sound practical to you?

I run a little pottery studio and want to stop guessing about cracking. Here's what I wrote in my notebook: "Does adding 5% grog by weight to our stoneware body reduce cracking in pieces thicker than 2 cm during bisque firing at a ramp of 100°C per hour?" I'd fire matched test tiles. Does this seem like a good question to you?

units: I'm a chef and I've been asked to speak at a food conference, which feels odd because I usually just cook. My opening: "Salt is the only rock we eat on purpose, and for ten thousand years we've argued about which ones taste best." What do you think?

I'm a line cook turned kitchen manager, 31, working on my first startup. Pitch: "We give restaurants a free fryer-oil sensor that tells them the day the oil actually goes bad instead of the day the schedule says, and we take a cut of the oil they save." Does that come across clearly? Curious what you think.

I run a Saturday knitting circle, and we're opening a cafe where each table has a basket of yarn and needles. The name is "Cast On," the first step of any project and an invitation to start something. Does it work for you?

Just finished this chorus and I'm kind of buzzing, so I'm sharing it right away. I'm a senior in high school, and it's about my town. Tell me what you think!
Everybody here knows my middle name and my mother's,
the truck my dad sold, the fence I drove through.
I'm leaving in June with one bag and no one's blessing.
God, I hope someplace else knows me half as well as you.

Here's my logline. I'm a long-haul trucker, 50, and I write in the cab at rest stops: "With six hours to his deadline, a trucker picks up a hitchhiker who can tell him exactly how many miles he has left to live, and it's fewer than the distance to his daughter's wedding." Thoughts?

I do alterations and slow-fashion tailoring, and I'm designing my logo. A yellow measuring tape curls into a spiral like a snail shell, its numbers getting smaller toward the middle. A small snail head and two feelers come out at the outer end. 'Slow Stitch' is stitched in dashes beneath it. I'm curious what you think.

I'm 16 and I made a plan for our tiny 1.5m x 3m balcony to help pollinators. West-facing, so hot. Back rail: lavender in long troughs. Middle tier: a 3-step shelf with creeping thyme, borage and calendula. Floor: a shallow saucer of pebbles and water for bees. Hanging baskets along the front with nasturtiums, trailing down so there's something flowering from April to October. Do you have any thoughts?

I'm a baker, so I'm up at 4am anyway. My cafe opens at 6:30 for the people on early shifts: bus drivers, midwives, cleaners. It's called "Half Past." You'd say, "Meet me at half past," and everybody knows it's an easy hour to get to. Just wondering what comes to mind when you read the name.

I own a flower shop and I'm training for my first marathon (week 10 of 16). Mon: rest. Tue: 8 miles easy. Wed: 6 miles with 3x1 mile at tempo. Thu: 5 easy plus strides, 20 min strength. Fri: rest. Sat: 16 mile long run, last 3 at goal pace. Sun: 4 recovery miles. Wedding season hits in May, so Fridays stay empty on purpose. What's your take?

I'm a 34-year-old home inspector, and I've been writing a horror screenplay on the side. Here's the logline: "A home inspector notices that every house in a new subdivision has one more room on the inside than on the outside, and the extra rooms are starting to be occupied." Be honest, what's your take?

units: Because I forget things, my budget is automated on payday (TA income $1,700). Rent $720 and utilities $55 autopay; $200 auto-savings; $60 'forgetful tax' fund for late fees and lost stuff; groceries $250; phone $35; transit $70; books $60; $200 weekly cash envelopes ($50 × 4) for fun; $50 buffer. What do you think of the system?

I'm a 20-year-old intern and somehow I was asked to speak for our founder. I said: 'I've known Mr. Reyes for eleven weeks. In that time he learned my name, my coffee order, and the name of my cat. I'm told he also started a company. I'll take people's word for it. But anyone who remembers the intern's cat has already built something that lasts.' Was that too bold?

Week 10 of my marathon block, aiming for 3:15. Mon: rest, 15 minutes of yoga. Tue: 8x400 m at 5k pace, 90 s jog. Wed: 10 km easy plus 6 strides. Thu: 16 km with 8 km at marathon pace (4:37/km). Fri: rest. Sat: 8 km easy, then 30 minutes of single-leg RDLs and calf raises. Sun: 30 km, last 5 at goal pace. About 85 km total. Would you change anything?

I'm an undergrad raising $3,000 to sequence soil from my grandmother's farm. Here's my opening, and I'm a bit anxious about it: "My grandmother says the south field is tired. I study microbes, so I asked what tired means. A teaspoon of that soil holds billions of organisms, and I'd like to find out which ones have quit." How does it land for you?

I knit as a hobby and I've been toying with a business idea. One sentence: "Knitters abandon sweaters at the sleeves because patterns don't fit their bodies, so we sell $14 pattern files that recalculate every stitch count from five measurements." Curious what you make of it, be as blunt as you like!

I'm a plumber and I came up with this for the side of my van: "Every house has one pipe that's been quietly holding a grudge since 1974." My wife says it's too long for a van. Be straight with me: would you read it, and would you call me?

History major here, posted this thread opener and I'm hoping for honest feedback: "The Library of Alexandria didn't burn in one dramatic night. It faded the way libraries do: budgets cut, scholars leaving, scrolls not recopied. Knowledge is lost less like a bonfire and more like a slow leak. Worth remembering when we trim library hours."

I'm a retired schoolteacher with an 8-inch telescope, and I posted this in my astronomy club's group: "Saturn tonight from the back garden. The rings were so sharp I could see the Cassini gap. I woke my wife to look. She said, 'It looks fake.' I said, 'That's the nicest thing anyone's said about it.'" Just a bit of fun, but I'd like your opinion.

I own three laundromats in Cleveland and I'm nervous about sharing this. My pitch: "I'll license the software I wrote that lets customers reserve a specific machine and get a text when their cycle ends, at $40 per location monthly, because it cut my idle machine time by 22%." Honest thoughts?

I'm putting this on the counter card at my bakery to get people to bring their own boxes: "Our croissants take three days to make. Their box takes three seconds to throw away. Bring your own container and we'll take 50 cents off, because anything worth waiting for deserves better than cardboard." Would this make you do it? Be blunt.

units: I do bookkeeping for small businesses on the side and I'm formalizing a resume for a staff accountant role. Here's the bullet I'm leading with: "Prepare books for 22 restaurants and salons; recovered $41K in sales-tax overpayments for clients in 2023 by reconciling POS exports against state filings." Would you change anything, or what's your impression?

I'm in an MFA program and workshopping this next week. Before I do, I'd like a fresh reader's take, especially on the line breaks:
The heron holds the river's one idea
so still the water starts to doubt itself.
Then the small bright argument
of a minnow, and the whole grey sentence
resolves into a throat.

I taught high school English for 34 years and now I'm learning dessert. Lemon posset: simmer 2 cups heavy cream with ¾ cup sugar for 3 minutes, then whisk in ⅓ cup lemon juice and 1 tbsp olive oil. Pour into glasses and chill for 4 hours. Serve with rosemary shortbread. The olive oil makes it taste silky and slightly grassy. Would you like to tell me what you think?

My partner and I are saving for a house. Combined take-home $9,800: rent 2,400; groceries 700; utilities 220; transit 300; insurance 180; house fund 2,500; index funds 1,800; dining and fun 900; travel 500; giving 300. Rule: if any category overspends, it borrows from fun, never from the house fund. What's your opinion?

Paralegal here, trying to move into litigation support. I'd love a second pair of eyes on this bullet: "Built a privilege-log template and tagging protocol that cut document review for a 400,000-page antitrust production from an estimated 9 weeks to 5, with zero clawback requests." What's your take?

I'm 81 and this is the first poem I've ever shown anyone. My granddaughter set up this chat for me. I'd be glad to hear what you think.
At eighty I price the stairs by breath:
the fourth one costs a nickel,
the ninth, a dime.
I reach the landing, solvent still,
and spend what's left on the window.

Quick one from a 26-year-old barista: "A court stenographer who has silently typed every word of eleven thousand trials is subpoenaed to testify, and discovers she is the only person who remembers what was actually said." What do you think? I'm planning to enter it in a screenwriting fellowship.

My used bookshop is called The Dog-Eared Page. For the logo, I imagined a simple page in cream, with its top corner folded down. The fold is shaped as a floppy dog ear, with one small ink dot for an eye on the folded part. Everything else is blank paper. Thoughts? Be as blunt as you like.

Hey, I'm a 45-year-old pediatric nurse, and I wrote this for a short film contest: "When a ten-year-old's imaginary friend begins aging faster than she does, she has one childhood left to keep him alive." Does it work as a logline? Any feedback welcome.

I'm 40 and a T10 paraplegic. I want to build strength without wrecking my shoulders. Mon: seated cable rows 4x10, face pulls 3x15, landmine press 3x8. Tue: handcycle intervals, 6x2 min hard/2 easy. Wed: rest. Thu: lat pulldowns 4x8, parallel-bar dips 3x6, rotator cuff band work. Fri: 30-minute steady handcycle. Sat: Pallof presses and core. Sun: rest. Pulling volume is double pushing on purpose. Thoughts?

units:
Hello, I'm a linguist and I wrote this edit distance function for comparing dialect spellings. It only keeps one row in memory:
```python
def levenshtein(a, b):
    prev = range(len(b) + 1)
    for i, ca in enumerate(a, 1):
        cur = [i]
        for j, cb in enumerate(b, 1):
            cur.append(min(prev[j] + 1, cur[j-1] + 1, prev[j-1] + (ca != cb)))
        prev = cur
    return prev[-1]
```
Could you give me your opinion?

Drafting a grant request for a long-term beetle survey and trying a bolder opening: "We're asking you to fund the least glamorous work in conservation: counting. You cannot protect what you cannot number. Our twelve-year survey is the only reason we knew the wetland was failing years before the herons left. Counting is how we hear a warning while it's still a whisper." Does it work as a first paragraph for a funder?

I'm a hospice night nurse, 43, and my coworkers encouraged me to write this down: "When a hospice nurse notices her dying patients all ask for the same stranger in their final hour, she tracks him down and finds a lonely locksmith who has never met any of them." Tell me what you think, please.

I own a little flower shop and wrote this on my lunch break. Showing it to you first, before anyone I know:
I can tell which bouquets will be forgiven
by how the man holds them:
like a question,
or like an alibi.
How does it read to you?

I'm a finish carpenter applying for a set builder job at a theater. Wrote this: "Furniture is built to last fifty years. A set is built to look like it will, for six weeks, and then be burned. I find that freeing. I can fake a hundred-year-old oak door from luan and one can of walnut stain, and I can make it survive a slammed exit every night." Does that work, do you think?

I'm an occupational therapist, and this is my layout for a sensory garden in a dementia care home. A looped path, 1.5m wide, with no dead ends, so no one gets stuck. Along it, five stations: scent (lavender, rosemary), touch (lamb's ear, grasses), sound (bamboo, wind chimes), taste (raspberries, mint) and a familiar-memory corner with a washing line and a shed. Handrails run along the edges, and the seating is every 12m. Would you give me your thoughts?

I work nights as a nurse and write on my breaks. Bit nervous to show anyone. This is how my story begins:
"The patient in bed nine had been dying politely for three weeks. He thanked us for the blankets, apologised for the trouble, and every night at three asked, very gently, whether we'd mind not letting the other man in. There was no other man. Bed ten was empty."
Honest thoughts?

I own a bike shop, and our mechanic Tomasz retires after 25 years. I'm proud of this one: "Tomasz can hear a loose bearing from across the shop and a lie from across the street. He fixed ten thousand flats and handed back every bike like it was new. Tomasz, we're keeping your bench exactly as it is, greasy thumbprints and all. Nobody's allowed to clean it." Thoughts?

Hi! I'm a line cook, six years in, applying for a sous chef job. Here's the middle paragraph of my letter: "At Marlow's I cut our walk-in waste from 14% to 5% by turning trim into the staff meal, then the staff meal into a Thursday special that outsold the ribeye. I'm not interested in cooking expensive food. I'm interested in making sure nothing that enters your kitchen dies in the bin." Honest thoughts?

I'm a retired electrician and this is my first poem since school. I wrote it about my mother's house:
I rewired my mother's house in 1987.
Behind the plaster, still, her wedding year:
cloth-wrapped cable, brittle as old licorice,
still carrying, without complaint,
the little the house had asked of it.
What would you say to it, honestly?

units: First-year law student. I told my study group: "The 'reasonable person' is the only one in law school who's never late, never confused, and has always done the reading." Everyone groaned in a good way, I think. What do you make of it?

I'm a freelance-turned-staff designer and the rebrand has ballooned. Does this email to my manager work?
"Hi Jo, the rebrand has grown from 6 deliverables to 14 since kickoff. All reasonable asks, but at my pace it lands three weeks late. Options: cut the packaging mockups, bring in Rafi for 10 days, or move the deadline to 21 June. I lean toward Rafi. Which do you prefer?"

I make a small podcast about local history from my closet, and I'm applying for a radio producer job. Here's the paragraph on my work. Can you tell me what you think?
"Episode 14 is eleven minutes about the 1952 flood, and nine of them are one woman, Dolores, describing the sound of the river at night. I cut my own questions to almost nothing. A producer's job, I've learned, is to build a quiet room and then leave it."

I do open mics on Thursdays as a hobby, and this is my new opener: "I slept wrong once in 2019 and my neck is still in litigation." I'm tempted to follow it with nothing, just let it sit. Does that instinct make sense? Genuinely curious.

A six-foot hedge of serviceberry and pussy willow sits in front of the hives to force a high flight path. A shallow water dish with pebbles sits 10 ft from the hives. Does it look sensible?
